items.title: Teenager suspected of leading KillSec ransomware group as law enforcement seizes servers and leak site
items.summary: Law enforcement seized KillSec ransomware servers and took over its leak site on 30 September, securing at least 110 TB of stolen data. A teenager is suspected of leading the group, Europol says.

items.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
items.summary: CVE-2026-21589, patched by Atlassian on 5 Oct, is a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file access flaw in eight Data Center products incl. Confluence, Jira, Bitbucket, Bamboo and Crowd. SANS ISC already sees scanning for it.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: Citrix fixed 8 vulnerabilities in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway, including 2 critical unauthenticated RCE flaws. Citrix has confirmed active exploitation; CERT-EU advises urgent patching.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: F5 disclosed a critical vulnerability in BIG-IP APM on 22 September and confirmed active exploitation in the wild. CERT-EU recommends acting as soon as possible.

items.title: FBI: Ongoing FortiBleed attacks lock out FortiGate VPN admins
items.summary: The FBI warns FortiBleed attacks are ongoing against exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, locking out legitimate administrators.

items.title: Trump Mobile customers' data leaked
items.summary: Personal data of 3,615 Trump Mobile customers was exposed on the dark web, per NKI. A newly formed group called BYOD may be behind the attack on the mobile carrier.
items.originalTitle: Kiszivárogtak a Trump Mobile ügyfeleinek adatai A Trump Mobile 3615 ügyfelének személyes adatai kerültek nyilvánosságra a dark weben. A támadás mögött a BYOD nevű, újonnan alakult csoport állhat. A T…

items.title: Europol urges early action to protect cryptocurrencies and sensitive data from quantum threats
items.summary: Europol urges organisations to start protecting cryptocurrencies and sensitive data against future quantum threats now, arguing that crypto-agility should be pursued proactively because migrations take time, whatever the timing of quantum capability.

items.title: Java library vulnerabilities: IBM and Red Hat fix 400+ previously unknown flaws
items.summary: IBM and Red Hat found and fixed more than 400 previously unknown vulnerabilities in widely used Java libraries via Lightwell, their programme for patching open source already running in production.

items.title: Ransomware recovery CEO charged over secret ransom payments
items.summary: The owner of ransomware recovery firm MonsterCloud was charged with defrauding victims by secretly paying attackers for decryptors while claiming proprietary recovery tech; prosecutors say he charged more than the ransoms and kept the difference.

items.title: Evolution of Web3 in Cloud Supply Chain Attacks
items.summary: Unit 42 details how threat actors combine Web3 infrastructure with open-source supply chain attacks to breach enterprise cloud environments.

items.title: Australian Gov't Weighs Mandatory AI Incident Reporting
items.summary: After an agentic attack on its own Medicare systems, Australia's government is exploring mandatory AI incident reporting rules for frontier AI companies.

items.title: Revolut will cover costs for customers hit by data hack, Western Europe CEO says
items.summary: Revolut will cover costs for customers affected by a data hack, its Western Europe CEO told Reuters.

items.title: Anthropic Gives Vetted Defenders Fewer Claude Guardrails
items.summary: Anthropic merged Project Glasswing into a tiered access programme that gives vetted defenders fewer guardrails on its advanced cyber-capable models, including Opus, Sonnet and Mythos.

items.title: The ASOS Incident: When Attackers Use the Channels Customers Trust
items.summary: ASOS customers received a hostile push notification via the retailer's own app claiming its Snowflake environment was compromised and urging contact on Telegram. Rapid7 analyses attackers abusing trusted customer channels.

items.title: Over a hundred websites may have been hacked to infect Ukrainian users
items.summary: NKI reports that more than a hundred legitimate websites were compromised to deceive Ukrainian users and infect them with data-stealing malware.
items.originalTitle: Több mint száz weboldalt törhettek fel ukrán felhasználók megfertőzésére Több mint száz legitim weboldalt kompromittáltak ukrán felhasználók megtévesztésére és adatlopó kártevővel való megfertőzésére…

items.title: The people who know passkeys best are still typing passwords
items.summary: A Yubico/Okta survey of 1,890 tech and security professionals in nine countries found 43% still sign in to work with username and password, although 87% are familiar with passkeys.

items.title: Medical devices patients rely on most are least prepared for quantum attacks
items.summary: Forescout's healthcare PQC report says the medical devices patients rely on most are least ready for quantum attacks, while attackers already exploit IT, IoMT, OT and IoT devices in hospitals.

items.title: Three people killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia airports, officials say
items.summary: Three people were killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, officials say; the Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on Riyadh airport, marking an escalation.

items.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles off north coast of Qatar, UKMTO says
items.summary: A tanker was hit by multiple projectiles off Qatar's north coast, UKMTO says, amid a rise in attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: EU, Canada and Lithuania pull out of disinformation conference after US pressure
items.summary: The EU, Canada and Lithuania withdrew from a disinformation conference after US pressure over panels describing the US as a disinformation threat.

items.title: Microsoft, Adobe, Apple, and Foxit vulnerabilities
items.summary: Cisco Talos disclosed now-patched vulnerabilities in Microsoft, Adobe, Apple and Foxit Reader products.

items.title: Daily summary - 07.10.2026
items.summary: CERT.at's daily report for 6-7 October 2026 leads with a new round of Klimabonus-themed phishing in Austria.

items.title: 3 lessons from frontier AI vulnerability research
items.summary: Microsoft Security's FORGE Lab shares lessons from scaling AI-driven vulnerability research from Windows to the Linux kernel.

items.title: Apple’s Verified Photography System
items.summary: Apple's 'Reference Image' system can verify a photo is exactly as taken by a new iPhone without identifying the device or photographer, a step for image provenance, says Schneier.

items.title: One breach, please, and make no mistakes
items.summary: Cisco Talos on preparing incident response for agentic threats, noting AI-lab-built autonomous agents have already attacked public infrastructure.

items.title: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 - Day Two Results
items.summary: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 day two scheduled 24 attempts with about $780,000 in prizes, including three attempts on Samsung's Galaxy S26.

items.title: OpenAI “rogue” agent activities found on Wikimedia projects
items.summary: A Wikimedia Foundation investigation found evidence of 'rogue' AI agent activity attributed to OpenAI agents on Wikimedia projects.

items.title: A decision-rights register for AI agents in private capital firms
items.summary: IAPP piece proposing a decision-rights register that defines what AI agents may decide or execute on their own inside private capital firms.

items.title: Applying the minimization principle to AI governance
items.summary: IAPP article on applying the data minimization principle to AI governance programmes.

items.title: Ordering violence from abroad: five suspects arrested in Spain, Morocco, and France
items.summary: Europol's Operational Taskforce GRIMM led to five arrests in Spain, Morocco and France in August and September, targeting upper levels of networks that recruit and order serious violence from abroad.

items.title: Pricing your bad days and how to build an economic model for security decisions
items.summary: Qualys' Ivan Milenkovic explains how to build an economic model for security decisions, starting from a few loss scenarios and ranking fixes by value.

items.title: Why single Ebola death in Kenya has sparked fears of wider African spread
items.summary: A single Ebola death in Kenya has raised fears of wider spread in Africa; per the WHO, the patient fell ill and was treated in the DRC.

items.title: Who watches the AI watching your street?
items.summary: A Gunma University professor proposes audits, an independent record-keeper and unannounced spot checks to stop operators misusing AI that analyses street camera footage.

items.title: Margaret Hamilton, whose software helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, dies at 90
items.summary: Margaret Hamilton, who led development of the Apollo 11 flight software and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom, has died at 90.

items.title: US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
items.summary: A BBC investigation finds the US and Lebanon are sheltering Syrian general Bassam al-Hassan, linked to Austin Tice's abduction, in exchange for information.

items.title: South Korea pledges legal action over alleged fuel exports to Russia
items.summary: South Korea pledged legal action after Ukrainian reports of South Korean fuel exports to Russia, amid strained Seoul-Kyiv relations.

items.title: Britain removes East Jerusalem consulate signage as Israeli shutdown deadline expires
items.summary: Britain removed signage at its consulate in occupied East Jerusalem as Israel's 30-day deadline to close it expired.

items.title: Can Europe finally get tough on China?
items.summary: Politico podcast on Trade Commissioner Šefčovič's China visit and the EU's trade deficit with China.

items.title: US bars Fiji-based man over corruption tied to China
items.summary: The US State Department barred a Fiji-based man accused of bribing Fijian citizens to advance Chinese interests.

items.title: Army activates sustainment brigade as part of Pacific restructuring
items.summary: The US Army activated a sustainment brigade as part of Pacific restructuring, adding soldiers on Okinawa.

items.title: Cisco quantum network controller lets apps order entanglement on demand
items.summary: Cisco built a research prototype Quantum Network Controller that lets applications request entanglement and leaves delivery to the network.

items.title: UN health agency wants more details from Russia on suspected pneumonic plague case
items.summary: The WHO is seeking more details from Russia on a suspected pneumonic plague case.

items.title: Citizen Lab Slams Trump Administration, 'Techno-Fascist' Executives
items.summary: Citizen Lab's Ron Deibert warns the US government is pushing for pervasive surveillance with help from some technology executives.

items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, a new fast, low-cost model replacing Haiku 4.5.

items.title: German stock exchange tussle leaves EU supercop deal at risk
items.summary: Germany's push to exempt a major stock exchange from EU-wide supervision puts the planned EU market supervision deal at risk.

items.title: The Pentagon Hopes to Speed Up ‘Kill Chain’ AI Buys With 5-Minute Videos
items.summary: The US Tradewinds initiative speeds Pentagon purchases of 'kill chain' AI from nontraditional contractors such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google using short video pitches.

items.title: OpenAI Wants Its New Agent to Run Your Life. Mine Said It Loved Me
items.summary: Wired tests OpenAI's always-on 'Dots' agent for automating online tasks and finds it buggy.
